title: Crestline Fleet Account Invoicing Standards
content:
Work charged to a Crestline Fleet Account becomes a fleet invoice. These standards govern how a ticket becomes an invoice and when it may be charged.

## 1. One invoice per ticket and service category

Work charged to a fleet account becomes one invoice per ticket and service category, so a ticket with tires and an alignment produces two invoices with their own invoice numbers; a road hazard certificate sold with tires is part of the tires invoice.

## 2. Conditions for charging

- The account must be in status active when a ticket is charged to it.
- The vehicle must be on the account's roster on the invoice date.

Both are read from the system records before the invoice posts: the status of the account charged, and the roster entries of that same account for that same vehicle. A driver's or the business's statement does not stand in for either record.

## 3. Discount and invoice amount

The discount amount is the program's fleet discount percent for the invoice's service category, applied to the ticket's pre-tax price excluding the items the discount never applies to, rounded half up to the cent; where the program uses the national fleet price file, tire prices are taken from the national fleet price file before the discount. The invoice amount is the ticket after the discount, plus the excluded items, plus sales tax unless the account is tax-exempt.

## 4. Purchase orders

A purchase order number is required when the account requires a purchase order on every ticket, or when the amount before tax is at or above the program's purchase order threshold; a ticket that needs a purchase order and has none cannot be charged.

## 5. Approval of large tickets

> A ticket above the account's ticket approval limit needs the fleet manager's approval before work starts.

This clause is **no longer in force** as an unqualified rule. The current basis reads: a ticket above the account's ticket approval limit needs the fleet manager's approval before work starts, except work that a driver may authorize alone in an emergency on a ticket a business disputes as an unapproved over-limit ticket; every other ticket remains under the approval requirement.

## 6. Credit limit

The ticket cannot be charged when it would take the outstanding balance above the credit limit plus the program's over-limit tolerance percent of that limit.

## 7. Due date

The due date is the invoice date plus the program's net terms days under per-invoice billing, or the month-end statement date plus the net terms days under monthly statement billing.

## 8. Mobile service visits

> A mobile service visit adds one visit fee invoice of the program's mobile service fee when that fee is above 0.00.

This clause is **no longer in force** as an unqualified rule. The current basis reads: for a visit fee a business contests through a visit fee dispute, and only for such a fee, the fee the visit owes is the fee the visit fee dispute rule works out from the program's mobile service fee; every other mobile service visit is invoiced under the clause above, adding one mobile service call invoice of the program's mobile service fee when that fee is above 0.00.

## Worked invoice (hypothetical ticket, tax-exempt account)

A Crestline Fleet Commercial account (tires discount 10 percent) charges a tire ticket with a pre-tax tire price of 600.00 and disposal fees of 15.00. The discount is 10 percent of 600.00, that is 60.00; the disposal fees are excluded from it. The invoice amount is 600.00 less 60.00, plus 15.00: 555.00, with no sales tax because the account is tax-exempt. The program's purchase order threshold is 0.00, so the ticket needs a purchase order number.
